title: Squinting Face with Tongue Emoji 😝 Meaning: Teasing
description: The squinting face with tongue emoji 😝 is a raspberry in emoji form: teasing, gloating, “eww” or giddy excitement. See how it differs from 😜 and 😛, with examples.
summary: 😝 has its eyes scrunched shut and its tongue out. It is the emoji version of blowing a raspberry. People use it to tease, to gloat after winning, to react to something gross or cringey, and to show giddy, can't-contain-it excitement. It is childish on purpose.
meaning: Picture a kid sticking out their tongue and going “nyah nyah.” That is the core of 😝. It shows up after a small victory (“got the last slice 😝”), after a playful refusal (“not telling 😝”), and whenever someone wants to be a brat in a way that is obviously affectionate. The squeezed-shut eyes give it more force than the open-eyed tongue faces, as if the sender is putting their whole face into it.

The same expression doubles as disgust. Scrunched eyes and a tongue out are also what people do when they taste something awful, so 😝 turns up as “bleh” or “yuck” in replies about bad food, sappy couples, or an embarrassing memory. It is a mild, comic kind of disgust. For real revulsion people pick 🤢 or 🤮, and 😝 is kept for things that are gross in a funny way.

It can mean excitement too. Among people who use it a lot, 😝 after good news reads as a squeal: “we're going to Disney 😝.” This use overlaps with 😆, and the two were often mixed up on older phones where the designs looked alike. If the sentence is happy and there is nobody to tease, the squeal reading is the right one.

Like the other classic tongue faces, it peaked when emoji keyboards were new and is used a bit less by teenagers today. It has not picked up any hidden or rude meaning along the way. What you see is what it means: someone being playful, loudly, in a way that would look silly on an adult face and is meant to.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Siblings, partners and close friends are the main audience. It lands after one-upmanship, a silly dare, or a refusal to share a secret. Because both eyes are closed, it does not carry the insinuation of a wink, which makes it safe for teasing family members or friends where flirting would be strange.

contexts.label: In gaming
contexts.body: After a win in a casual game with friends, 😝 is light trash talk. It says “beat you” without the edge that 💀 or a clown would add. In competitive chats with strangers it can still irritate, because gloating is gloating, but among friends it keeps the rivalry friendly.

contexts.label: In captions
contexts.body: Photos of people actually pulling this face get captioned with it, along with posts about sour candy, spicy food challenges and anything involving a silly dare. It is also common on photos of kids and pets with their tongues out, where it simply mirrors what is in the picture.

examples.text: Too slow, I already called shotgun 😝
examples.meaning: Gloating over a small win in a playful, sibling-style way.

examples.text: Not telling you what I got you, you'll have to wait 😝
examples.meaning: Teasingly refusing to reveal a surprise.

examples.text: They were feeding each other fries the whole dinner 😝
examples.meaning: Mock disgust at a couple being overly cute in public.

examples.text: Tried the pickle soda. Never again 😝
examples.meaning: Something tasted bad, reported with humor instead of real distress.
Giddy excitement the sender can barely hold in.

examples.text: Told you I'd beat your high score 😝
examples.meaning: Friendly bragging after winning a game.

combos.meaning: Rubbing in a win, usually over something minor like a board game.
Something was extremely sour; the face mimics the pucker.
Embarrassed giggling about something the sender said or did.

confusedWith.difference: 😜 keeps one eye open in a wink, which adds a knowing, sometimes flirty note aimed at the reader. 😝 shuts both eyes and is louder and more childish, with no innuendo attached.
😆 has the same scrunched eyes but a wide laughing mouth and no tongue. It means hearty laughter. 😝 swaps the laugh for a stuck-out tongue, turning the reaction into a taunt or a “bleh.”
😋 has its tongue at the corner of a smile and means something is delicious. 😝 is the reverse when used about food: tongue straight out, eyes screwed up, something tasted terrible.

avoid: Do not gloat with it when the other person is really upset about losing or missing out.
Avoid it in serious or professional messages, since it reads as childish by design.
Skip it as a reaction to food someone cooked for you unless they will clearly take “yuck” as a joke.
design: A yellow face with eyes clamped shut into X-like or angled lines and a tongue sticking straight out of an open, grinning mouth. The official Unicode name spells it out as a face with stuck-out tongue and tightly closed eyes. Vendors draw the squint a little differently, some as a sharp > < shape and others as curved lines, but the expression is consistent.

faqs.a: Less than the other tongue faces. With both eyes shut there is no wink and no suggestive look, so it mostly reads as silly. It can still be part of flirting when two people tease each other a lot, but the emoji alone does not signal romance.
Sometimes. After a mention of bad food, something cringey or an overly mushy moment, it means “eww” in a joking way. After a brag or a refusal, it is a taunt. The sentence before it tells you which.

faqs.q: How can I tell 😝, 😛 and 😜 apart?
faqs.a: All three stick out a tongue. 😛 has open eyes and is the mildest. 😜 winks, adding a teasing or flirty hint. 😝 squeezes both eyes shut and is the most exaggerated, used for gloating, squealing or mock disgust.

It is cheeky, not rude. Sticking out your tongue at a friend is a joke; doing it to someone who is angry with you is a provocation. The emoji follows the same rule, so save it for people who know you are playing.
